answers.description: A Model Context Protocol server that reads data from a FreeStyle glucose sensor.

intent.goal: Expose a FreeStyle continuous glucose monitor to an AI agent over MCP, covering both real-time reads (current value and trend) and historical analysis (windows and aggregates), with no manual export step.
intent.users: Open source, aimed at other people living with diabetes who use a FreeStyle sensor and an MCP-capable agent. Each installation is self-hosted and bound to a single sensor account.
constraints: Health data — readings and credentials stay local; nothing leaves in clear, nothing is committed.
Not a medical device — informational only; no treatment decision may depend on it.
nonGoals: No writing and no dose calculation — read-only.
No UI or dashboard — the MCP server is the only interface.
No multi-user support — one sensor account per installation.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP tools work end to end: a current-glucose tool and a history-over-N tool both return real sensor data from Claude.
A third party installs it in under 10 minutes following the README alone.
No secret and no real reading anywhere in the repo; credentials via env vars / local config; .gitignore verified.
Units (mg/dL and mmol/L) and timezones handled explicitly and correctly.
